reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows in 20-30 feet over brush.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow early and a topwater or wake bait close to shore is working well. Later, move out off the dam and work those schools of bass with a clear topwater or tiny swimbait to get bites.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows. Largemouth bass are good on hard and soft plastics on shorelines and ledges.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are slow during the day and only a little more active at night. Crappie are numerous on timber and brush piles between 15-25 feet deep. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie fishing is excellent anywhere from 8-30 feet of water on timber. Fish shaded areas along retaining walls with coneheads and clousers for bass. Fish weedless streamers around vegetation for bass during the evenings.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Full summertime pattern with crappie in 15-32 feet of water.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Stripers, channel catfish, and black bass remain slow overall, but bank fishing has been good throughout the lake using fishbites, tilapia, and dead cut bait.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair on dock poles and brush piles. Largemouth bite is decent using jigs, deep crankbaits, and wacky rigged baits near deep docks and points. White bass bite is good and hybrids are fair on main lake humps with slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.35 pounds are slow in 8-25 feet of water on trick worms and square bill cranks. Crappie are good to 13 inches on minnows and jigs in 10-18 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with a consistent offshore bite. With the water at 82 degrees, expect good activity from warm-water species like bass and panfish.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow, but redfish continue to be productive around Spider Island and Picnic Point using tilapia, cut bait, fishbites, and a variety of flavored baits.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: A good go-to setup includes a variety of slabs, spinnerbaits and the always-reliable yellow bladed Bo Blade spinner using the proven saw tooth retrieve technique.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck's Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have moved deeper but big catfish are in the shallows. Bass bite is inconsistent and hit or miss. Bass and crappie are doing best with shiners.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair, with fish holding around timber in 8-10 feet of water, and some extended points producing the fish early in the day.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: As the summer temperatures increase, target crappie are in deeper timber along the river channel and brush piles.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are slow during the day and only a little more active at night. Crappie are numerous on timber and brush piles between 15-25 feet deep. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow on chartreuse and white slabs. Crappie are slow around boat docks but a few are being caught on deep water brush piles with minnows and jigs. Black bass are estimated to be slow to fair early in the mornings and late in the evenings.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Topwater bass bite is good the last 2 hours of daylight using poppers and frog patterns.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good in brush about 12 feet deep on minnows and jigs. Bass fishing is slow and only good in shallow water. Sand bass fishing is good on slabs and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass and sand bass are good on slabs and live shad on the lower ends. Some largemouth bass are on the surface early and late and are good on crankbaits and soft plastics. Look for the bigger largemouth near creek entrances and near shaded docks later.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 6 pounds. Crappie are good to 2 pounds on jigs tipped with Berkley Crappie Nibbles. White bass are fair on slab spoons fished over main lake humps.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Fish early and late for bream and bass in and around weed beds with small poppers.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are improving on the main river channels, with minnows and hand-tied jigs producing great catches around brush. Largemouth bass are setting up well around boat docks and deeper letdowns, biting crankbaits, grubs, and spinnerbaits. White bass are becoming more consistent on the lower end of the lake and at the old road bed, hitting divers and pet spoons on a 3 inch leader as well as slabs fished vertically on jumps off the old channel.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting slow, and fishing has been tough.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are sporadically busting on shad all over the lake. A medium size swimbait can be used to pick off bass that are suspended in the trees.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have slowed down with some days they're munching, some days they are statues and don't move a muscle, and then some days it's "where are they?" Black bass are good with white and chartreuse spinnerbaits being super fun in the mornings along with jerkbaits and soft plastics like the original Slugo worked Texas rigged without a weight, twitching it making it dance underneath the surface. White slabs 1 ounce with all the treble hooks cut off except one makes life easier. Tying a jig around 12 inches above your slab on a loop knot, you will catch two fish at a time.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 15-20 feet of water with minnows and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinners, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 15-28 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 8-14 feet of water on minnows. Largemouth bass are good on docks, bulkheads, and brush piles in 4-14 feet of water with Texas rigs, Carolina rigs, chatterbaits, and spinnerbaits. White bass are good on silver War Eagle Super Slabs in 7-17 feet of water on humps, points, and flats.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good off points with brush in 25 feet using big worms with shaky heads. Crappie are fair using minnows around standing timber in 18-25 feet.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have improved to fair in 3-4 feet of water. Bass are good pitching creature baits and plastic worms shallow and in hardwoods.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been fishing excellent on medium diving crankbaits and Carolina rigs with big worms anywhere around 15-22 feet of water around creek channel swings. Crappie have been fishing good on white and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass fishing is good on Carolina rigs and medium diving crankbaits in 15-20 feet of water around deep drop-offs off of points. Crappie fishing has been excellent on white and chartreuse jigs in the standing timber.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass bite has been good flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The bass are staying in the shallows but seeking the shadiest places possible around reeds. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: Riley Hindes, Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting great in open water, on brush piles, and off the docks. A lot of 5-7 pound largemouth bass are being caught by accident, usually on minnows while fishing for crappie and catfish.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 6 pounds with one 10 pounder reported caught on a chatterbait. Most bass are being caught on topwater and shallow flooded bushes. Some bass are in 10-14 feet on a 10-inch worm on long tapering points. Crappie are slow with scattered reports off deeper trees scattered mid lake on minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting slow in deep water 15-20 feet on minnows. Black bass, hybrids and sand bass are really slow and haven't done too good this year.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is fair on large swimbaits and dropshots around grass lines in about 15 feet of water. Crappie fishing is fair with some numbers but not a lot of big ones right now.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and relating to brush piles in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are a little slow right now with plenty of fish but they're just not aggressive. Live shad is the best for that, but you can still slab them. Largemouth bass can be caught offshore in 12-18 feet of water on rocks which has been better than any other structure. Bass are trying to get protection from the sun, so any flooded grasses, buck brush, willows, or laydowns are better shallow. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair with fish being caught on slabs on points, humps and roadbeds. Crappie action is slow with a few fish coming on minnows on brush piles, timber and bridge columns in 20 feet of water. Black bass can be caught on main lake boat docks throughout the day.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Conditions are changing quickly with bass moving to points, humps and offshore structure due to water releases. Crappie are fair.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are good on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water with late afternoon bite good. Black bass are slow on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still scattered, but some nice ones are being caught deep and shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great in the shallows around the flooded vegetation and are destroying topwater baits such as frogs, etc.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Live shad and slab spoons are working equally good. The crappie bite has picked up. The largemouth bite is good on frogs at daylight and working over to shallow cranks around dock legs and submerged irrigation intakes.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good under 59 bridge and 172 bridge. Catfish are good all over and bass are fair in Sandy's Creek and Navidad River.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are holding tight to structure and brush in 18-25 feet of water using minnows dead or alive.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair. Some good bass can be caught in 10-14 feet on Texas rig worms and shallow running crankbaits. Crappie fishing is just tough.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been caught on minnows in 16-20 feet of water on brush piles. Bass have been good on topwater, worms, and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacked on brush in 15 feet of water. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on crankbaits and jigs around docks and rocks. Crappie are fair with minnows and jigs on brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up in the main lake in brush in 15-30 feet of water. White bass fishing is fair on slabs on main lake humps in 25-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass fishing is good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in grass in 8-12 feet of water with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko worms and crankbaits. Bass are good on brush in 15-18 feet of water with spoons and Texas rig worms. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Throwing a topwater frog first thing in the morning over the top of the grass has been good for bass. After the sun rises, target bass on deep shaded shorelines or under deeper shaded docks.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie is good on structure using live minnows and jigs. Hybrid striped bass is good on live bait on humps and ledges in 20-40 feet of water using live bait and slabs.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Catching lots of spotted and small largemouth around the structure but the bigger fish have slowed down. Crappie have also slowed but can be picked off of timber. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Flyfishing for bass should produce bass with Dock knockers and small closures around retaining walls. Crappie continue to congregate on structure, schooling on timber in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with pond weed early with frogs, flukes, buzz baits on the edge 2-4 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass activity remains slow, and catfish have also been hit-or-miss.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 3 pounds are slow in 3-15 feet of water on wacky rig senkos on the dock poles and topwater frogs in the shoreline grass. Crappie are slow to 11 inches on minnows and jigs in 10-18 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with a consistent offshore bite.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Bass and striper are slow.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action has been fast at times, and freshwater drum are also being caught from the bank.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been slow, but anglers are having the most luck using soft plastics with a hint of red.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to poor, holding tight to brush piles and submerged timber in 15-25 feet, with slow minnows or jigs working best. Largemouth bass are active on deeper structure in 10-20 feet and schooling early and late around shad pods - perfect for crankbaits, swimbaits, or topwaters. Hybrid stripers are hitting slabs, spoons, and live shad on flats and drop-offs in 14-30 feet.
reports.by: Bradly Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: A few smaller carcasses and some bass remains were also found in the dumpster, suggesting a productive outing.
reports.by: Weber’s Landing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sandbass angling continues to be good on trolled baits and slabs worked near feeding flats on many areas of the lake. Numerous small striped bass and some largemouth bass are schooling with sandbass. Largemouth bass are fair to good on soft plastics, spinners and crankbaits.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: The main lake is in great condition, and early morning largemouth bass are hitting chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, and Texas-rigged worms on shallow structure and flats. Crappie turning on in 6-10 feet water, holding tight to structure and biting minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinners, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 15 to 28 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with best times early and late afternoon. The outer edge of the hydrilla is holding bass and deep brush using texas rigged and shaky head worms. Crappie are good in 25-30 feet of water suspended around brush piles.
reports.by: Hambone fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been excellent on creek channel swings using Carolina rigs and drop shots, with groups of 15-30 fish stacked up in the middle of the lake - most running 2-4 pounds, and you can often catch 5 or 6 before they scatter. Crappie action has been hit-or-miss - big ones are tight to standing timber, while smaller keepers are holding on brush piles off secondary points, with 1/32 ounce white jigs being the go-to.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie numbers are solid, though catfish have been slow.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being caught on small swimbaits and 12-15 feet of water in drains and pockets slowly rolled off the bottom. Bass reported to 6.5 pounds. Crappie are slow but they are being caught if you can work and move around to various trees in the clear water mid to Lower Lake.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and deep biting minnows. Few reports of bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and relating to brush piles 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White Bass are fair with a few being caught on slabs on main lake points, humps and roadbeds in 15 feet of water.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catching lots of spotted and small largemouth around the structure but the bigger fish have slowed down. Crappie have also slowed but can be picked off of timber. At the Marina crappie bite is fair.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappies are slow. Bass are slow with very few anglers on the water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and bass are fair north of Highway 59.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good near points and along the edges of the coves near the south end of the lake. Crappie have started hitting the shade and the 15-18 feet of water near docks and in brush piles.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on live minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Catching numbers of small bass on points, but the larger bass are slow. Crappie are good on deep timber with jigs and minnows. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Flyfishing for bass should produce bass with Dock knockers and small clousers around retaining walls. Crappie continue to congregate on structure, schooling on timber in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught early in the morning in pond weed with popping frogs, or poppers at the edge of grass. Bass are good with Texas rigs, creature baits or beavers around big timber and old road beds in 3-7 feet. Crappie limits are still possible but will take some time.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair on dock poles and brush piles. Largemouth bass bite is decent using jigs, crankbaits, and soft plastic baits near docks and rock points, white bass bite is good and hybrids are fair on main lake humps with slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6 pounds are slow in 3-15 feet of water on big soft plastics, wacky rig senkos and Hag’s Outlier Frogs in the shoreline grass. Crappie are good to 11 inches on minnows and jigs in 10-18 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are fair to 1.5 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Lake conditions are good as current continues to flow from Lake of the Pines, so the schooling bass action is starting to heat up.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: A good go-to setup include a variety of slabs, spinnerbaits and the always-reliable yellow bladed Bo Blade spinner using the proven saw tooth retrieve technique.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: However, bank fishing has been excellent, especially for crappie, white bass, and both blue and channel catfish.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is fair at best, with most action coming on soft plastics fished off extended points and around timber in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are producing well around docks, offshore structures, and bream beds, with crankbaits and soft plastics working best. Crappie fishing is fair to poor, with fish holding near submerged structures in 15-25 feet of water. Hybrid stripers are biting well on slabs, spoons, and live bait over flats and drop-offs in 12-30 feet.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Catching numbers of small bass on points, but the larger bass are slow. Crappie are good on deep timber with jigs and minnows. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and docks but you will have to weed through numbers of small fish to catch a limit.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are good on slabs and shallow water crankbaits under the lights. Crappie are fair in deep water brush piles on jigs.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with frogs, buzz baits and poppers early morning on points and grass lines or around pond weed. Fish this type of cover at mid day when bass are seeking cover. Small fish patterns like a dock knocker are producing bass and crappie shallow near grass. Lake Fork crappie fishing is in a summer pattern with fish loaded up on brush piles, laydowns and trees. We are still weeding through a tremendous number of short crappie, but this means the future of crappie fishing is looking very good.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water vegetation. Crappie are good in brush about 10 feet deep.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in numbers and many are schooling with the sand bass on feeding flats in town to Blue Water shores. Some of the bigger largemouth are near creek entrances and deeper docks. Best baits for largemouth are spinner baits and crankbaits early with soft plastics working later in the morning. Crappie reports are mixed, but small minnows and jigs worked near underwater structures like flooded timber from Water’s Edge to Bentwater are reported as good.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are holding steady on docks, riprap, and drains, biting well on Texas-rigged Rage Craws and chatterbaits. Crappie are good in the East Fork though the bite is light - minnows and silver hand-tied jigs are producing at 8-14 feet.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics and jigs on brush and structure at any depth above the thermocline. Schooling bass can be caught with rattletraps, swimbaits, and topwaters.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on shallow flats next to deep water with lipless crankbaits and square bill crankbaits. Crappie are good on slip cork minnows or jigs 12-15 feet of water on brush piles and timber.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 9-25 feet of water on timber and brush. White bass are good in 15-20 feet on main lake points all day with a 1 ounce white or chartreuse slab bounced off the bottom. Most slabs come with treble hooks, but if you cut all but one hook off it will make getting fish off the hook easier. Black bass are really good in the mornings on red, or chartreuse and white spinnerbaits in 7 feet of water. Target bass around boat ramps, underwater rock, piles, flooded brush, and any of the riprap. Live Scope with a swimbait over crappie piles is super fun right now. Lots of bass in the 10-20 feet range in the piles.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 15-28 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Ducktracker slabs have been the ticket. Largemouth have been good on swim jigs and hitting rocks on wind blown points with square bill crank baits.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good early and late along the edge of the hydrilla. Crappie are good in brush piles and standing timber with bottom depth 25-30 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good, with sand bass being caught all over the lake - gray or pink jig-heads with red eyes paired with pearl blue or pearl white grubs are producing well. White jerkbaits, rattling shad, and minnows have also been effective for both largemouth and smallmouth. Crappie fishing is fair, with catches coming from the Sanford Yake area, Blue West, and the shallows around Fritch Fortress.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in 13-20 feet of water on deep diving crankbaits and Carolina rig or Texas rig. Crappie are excellent on small chartreuse or white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on large swimbaits or Carolina rigs along grass lines. Crappie are good on 1/32 ounce chartreuse or white crappie jigs in the laydowns in the timber fields.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 7 pounds on Hags outlier frogs and newly flooded brush working best. Bass can be caught on small worms and creature baits 5 feet or less. Crappie are slow with some being reported around Bluffs around Lee Day, Cemetery Hole and in front of Ranger Cove.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to bite in deeper water on minnows.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Carolina rigs and dropshots around grass lines. Crappie are fair with white, clear or chartreuse crappie jigs in large brush piles.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on brush piles in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing are fair and the water is stained and 86 degrees.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are settling into typical summer patterns, with activity picking up around deeper structure and points. Crappie are also being found around brush piles, though the bite can be spotty at times.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina crappie are fair, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, and catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Crappie are good in the late afternoon on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Black bass are slow on crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Bass are slow with very few anglers on the water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Look for largemouth bass in flooded terrestrial vegetation.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Best lures have been the slab spoon, but live shad is also working. Crappie are decent on minnows on bridge pylons and submerged brush piles in 10-15 feet. Largemouth are good on senkos, square bills and frogs.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is up and down with the weather.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Night fishing for bass has been the most productive, especially around last week’s full moon - good numbers of quality fish were caught on Texas and Carolina-rigged 10-12 inch worms and lizards, with a few also hitting spinnerbaits and buzzbaits near lighted docks close to deep water. A few bass are being picked up shallow on frogs in heavy lily pads, though bites are limited. Crappie are extremely slow, with many guides canceling trips over the next couple of weeks.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair with primarily undersized fish with some keepers in 12-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are good in 6-7 feet of water on grass and shaded structure with plastic worms and topwaters. Crappie have been in two main patterns with most fish 20 feet deep, but there is a good number of fish in 8-12 feet of water on brush piles. Bass are great at dawn and dusk on topwater, but this bite shuts off very quickly.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: The clarity is muddy and the bite will be tough for white bass, crappie and bass. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Bass are slow on soft plastics or crankbaits in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on main lake brush piles in 15-30 feet of water. White bass are fair on slabs on main lake humps in 25-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good on soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught with deep diving crankbaits on deep points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are schooling in the evenings on flats in 15-22 feet of water biting small green plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair at night feeding under lights and active at day break. Crappie slow to fair between 15-25 feet deep on any structure above the thermocline. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Flyfishing for bass should produce bass with Dock knockers and small clousers around retaining walls. Crappie continue to congregate on structure, schooling on timber in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Early morning bass bite is fair with flukes and frogs near pond weed in 2-4 feet. Crappie limits are still possible but will take some time.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5 pound are good in 3-15 feet of water on big soft plastics on deep brush, wacky rig senkos, Hag’s swim jigs and Outlier Frogs in the shoreline grass. Crappie are good to 11 inches on minnows and jigs in 10-18 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles. White bass are good to 1.5 pounds on crappie jigs and crank baits out of the lights at night with some schooling early and late.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass schooling activity has started to improve, as well as the topwater frog bite around the lily pads. You can catch the bass chasing shad on flukes, worms, pop r’s, ploppers, buzz baits and small swimbaits. The river has cleaned cleared and the current slowed. down some the bass will be schooling and can be caught on Texas rig worms and drop shots plus top water.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been good on offshore structures and docks as well as schooling on shad in up to 30 feet of water. Crappie have been poor overall with minimal numbers being caught. Hybrids are active on flats and drop-offs in 12-32 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and live bait.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair at night feeding under lights and active at day break. Crappie slow to fair between 15-25 feet deep on any structure above the thermocline. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and docks but you will have to weed through numbers of small fish to catch a limit.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to good on chartreuse and white slabs in 15-20 feet of water on ridges south of Pelican Island. Crappie are fair to good on jigs or live bait on brush piles and rock piles.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Grass is looking good, so cast a frog to see if you can get a bass to bite. Bass are good 20 feet of water biting deep diving crankbaits, shaky heads and Carolina rigs.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Fish this type of cover at mid day when bass are seeking cover. Small fish patterns like a dock knocker are producing bass and crappie shallow near grass. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been super up and down this past week.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow flipping shallow water. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs in shade and brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are a bit deeper and a shaky head works wonders on this lake around offshore humps and ledges.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: The best reports of fish are the white bass which are being caught all over the lake on slabs, spinnerbaits and trolled baits. Largemouth bass are abundant and are good to 7 pounds fished near creek entrances. Best largemouth bass action is on spinnerbaits and crankbaits early then soft plastics later in the day. Crappie reports have been slow to fair on jigs fishing on bridge pilings and underwater timber.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow. Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Now, or in the near future is the time to smack the crappie on the flats off the main channels in 8-14 feet of water tight to structure. Largemouth bass are starting to group up on docks and can be targeted in drains, or rocks near deeper water eating grubs, worms, crankbaits and chatterbaits. White bass are slowly gathering on humps and sandbars hitting pet spoons and vertical jigging slabs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics on brush and structure in 8-20 feet with a dropshot, Texas rig, shaky head.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be found shallow during the early morning hours before the sun gets up. Crappie are out on your favorite summer deep spots on minnows.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on crankbaits in 10-15 feet of water with Carolina rigs or white flukes. Crappie are holding in isolated brush piles and laydowns in 12-14 feet of water with slip cork minnows, or ⅛ ounce jigs pink head with white chartreuse minnow will work if using live scope. Channel catfish are holding around the same cover as the crappie just closer to the bottom.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Before the recent flooding bass could be caught skipping deeper docks with jigs, flukes and worms.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Fresh willow tree piles are best for crappie right now they need to be set in 17 feet of water. Largemouth bass continue to be good in 4-14 feet of water with boat docks, bulkheads, and rocks with chatterbaits, Texas rigs, Carolina rigs, and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early morning and late afternoon. Crappie are fair to good suspended in brush and standing timber in 25-30 feet. This also affects bass and crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: White jerkbaits, rattling shad, and live minnows are working great for both largemouth and smallmouth bass. Crappie are good in the Sanford Yake area, off the docks, and in shallow waters around Bugbee and Blue West.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in 15-20 feet of water on deep diving crankbaits and Carolina rigged with large creature baits. Crappie are excellent for numbers on deep brush piles, and for size on standing timber in the center of the lake north of the powerlines.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass good to 5 pounds in newly flooded vegetation on topwater frogs, ploppers, chatterbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are on the move with the new water.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent big swimbaits and dropshots schooling in the center of the lake. Crappie are good with white crappie jigs in large brush piles.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and relating to brush piles 12-18 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns and they are moving around drop off going from structure to structure.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: This will keep some big bass in those coves.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: There is still water spilling over the spillway and the current is attracting the bait fish and in turn the sandies, bass and catfish. Crappie are slow. Bass are slow with very few anglers on the water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: If largemouth bass are schooling on the surface, there will likely be white bass mixed in. Before flooding conditions bass were schooling around the trees and bigger bends on the lake and willow points biting small swimbaits or topwaters.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good on hard baits and reaction baits near docks and the backs of coves early in the mornings and late evenings. Striped bass are good on topwaters in shallow water, switching to slabs as fish move out to 15 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough with a few bites at daylight on topwater and swim jigs. Crappie are hit-and-miss on main lake docks and brush piles.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: When conditions become safe again target Guadalupe bass on cliffs, rocks and deeper ledges in 10-20 feet. Largemouth are in the grass areas from mid lake to lower end. Find the grass, find the bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-12 feet of water on brush piles with watermelon gray chartreuse with glitter, or live minnows. Black bass are fair. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie good on jigs and minnows 18 feet.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling on baitfish around creek mouths with a good bite on weightless flukes, small walking baits and poppers. Bass are also good around brush piles out in 10-20 feet of water with big worms, jigs and small minnows.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Lake Bastrop schooling bass are good throwing small clear topwaters, small swimbaits in shad colors on a tiny ball jig head, underspins, a small belly weight hook, or drag a shaky head with a watermelon based color trick worm. A Carolina rigged fluke or finesse worm works great on the ledges and a frog around the reeds can land a bigger bass. There is some schooling action in the evenings, but the bass are finicky. Bass are good with clear topwaters and beetle spins early morning and late.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on soft plastics and crankbaits. Crappie are good on minnows.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are plentiful and patrolling structure in the 20 foot range. Crappie can be caught in large numbers on timber and brush just above the thermocline. Crappie are biting minnows mainly. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Check out the backs of coves for hydrilla and milfoil, fish patterns should draw bass out from cover. Crappie continue to congregate on structure, schooling on timber in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early around pond weed with frogs, and rage swimmers. Bass are good offshore in 15-26 feet on brush piles, rock, pond dams and long flats with bushes fish the drop off spot with big worms, and big creatures baits. Crappie limits are still possible but will take some time.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the morning then become sluggish as the days heats up. Largemouth bass are good off main lake points and rocks using Texas rigs and deep crankbaits. Hybrids and white bass are good using slabs and live shad on main lake humps. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4 pounds are slow in 3-15 feet of water on big soft plastics on deep brush, Hag’s swim jigs in the shoreline grass, crankbaits and topwaters. Crappie are fair to 11 inches on minnows and jigs in 18-25 feet on deeper large docks with brush on the main lake and on scattered brush piles in 8-18 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: After catching some water bass are shallow over rocks in 5-15 feet of water throwing crankbaits, swimbaits, frogs or soft plastics such as flukes, worms and craw worms. Throwing moving baits like crankbaits and jerkbaits will get a lot of bites from those and largemouth as well. Crappie are fair in 20-25 feet of water on brush piles and standing timber with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Have a topwater or a fluke on deck if you see the bass schooling. Worm patterns will be good as the temperatures increase and bass move deeper. Bass can also be targeted under grass and lily pads so have that frog, Look for the bait popping or listen to the lily pads as they will tell you if there is bait around.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing is a great option right now, with excellent catfish action along with good catches of crappie and freshwater drum.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with most catches coming on red shad soft plastics in 5-10 feet of water around stumps and submerged trees.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are plentiful and patrolling structure in the 20 foot range. Crappie can be caught in large numbers on timber and brush just above the thermocline. Crappie are biting minnows mainly. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and docks but you will have to weed through numbers of small fish to catch a limit.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to good on chartreuse and white slabs in 15-20 feet of water on ridges south of Pelican Island. Crappie are fair to good on jigs or live bait on brush piles and rock piles. Bass Report by Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Bass fishing is great on rocks in 8-15 feet of water with Texas rig plastics and deep diving crankbaits.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good 20 feet of water biting deep diving crankbaits, shaky heads and Carolina rigs.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early morning around grass with frogs, buzz baits and poppers. Fish this type of cover at midday when bass are seeking cover. Drop a clouser on an isolated cover for black bass. Lake Fork crappie fishing is improving as we enter the summer pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good on walkways near shorelines with soft plastics, and bigger brush piles off docks with soft plastics. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs in shade and brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Schooling sandbass are numerous and are good on little georges, in-line spinners and slabs. Largemouth bass are good to 7lbs on main lake points and in the back of sloughs chasing shad.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good in 3-8 feet of water around structure with various baits. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows in 5-10 feet of water over brush.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on humps with slabs.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are still holding near drains and are beginning to stack up on docks and deeper structure, with solid bites coming on weedless grubs rigged with 3/16-1/4 ounce weights and spinnerbaits. Crappie are hugging tight to structure in 8-12 feet of water and require a bit of finesse to trigger bites.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on deeper brush and shaded docks with soft plastics. Crappie are on deep brush biting minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good with soft plastics in brush piles. Crappie are on brush piles biting minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting on jigs and soft plastics in 6-15 feet on brush and structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great in 3-6 feet of water on hard structure and flooded solitary brush and stumps with shallow square bill crankbaits in crawfish red. Crappie can be caught in 7-9 feet of water on laydowns, or on deep piles in 25 feet. If fish are not surfacing use a 1 ounce white slab.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on docks and bulkheads in 3-10 feet of water skipping a light jig or Texas-rigged fluke or worm. Bass are good around submerged grass on chatterbaits and a Texas rig worm, or around brush piles and rock piles dragging a worm.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair fishing along the hydrilla with Texas rigged plum colored worms. Crappie are good with minnows.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: White jerkbaits, rattling shad, and live minnows are working great for both largemouth and smallmouth bass. Crappie are biting well in the Sanford Yake area, off the docks, and in shallow waters around Bugbee and Blue West.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent with June bug colored Carolina rigged baits, and medium diving crankbaits. Crappie are fair with big groups on brush piles, but bigger fish in standing timber North of the power lines.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are suspended in 8 feet of water, with some bigger fish being caught off the bottom in 8-10 feet. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with topwaters and big worms on trees. Crappie are excellent on deep brush piles and deep timber with crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 9 pounds possible. Some good bass being caught with red bug or plum 10 inch worms. Crappie bite is good with some limits reported on minnows and small jigs. Most crappie are suspended around bigger tree stumps or next to a river ledge 5-18 feet depending on the depth of the trees.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the brush.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good near main lake points on grass lines with dropshots and Carolina rigs. Crappie are good on clear and white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are in 18-25 feet of water primarily on rock piles with 10 inch worms, crankbaits and football jigs. The best bass bite is flipping shallow cover early in the morning. Crappie are good in brush piles and timber in 18-25 feet of water. Sand bass are on humps and points in 20-25 feet of water with slabs. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Topwater or a glide bait shallow early should produce some bass, then target docks around points on the main lake after that.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Topwater bass bite is early in the morning and evening. Bass are deeper on points, drains and humps with crankbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are good on brush piles, but many undersized fish and bluegill to sift through.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, and the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait and bluegill are fair on crickets or worms. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Black bass are slow on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: This typically attracts the bait fish to the current and in turn the sandies, bass and catfish. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Hybrid striper and white bass are good on swim baits, slab spoons and live bait in 17-35 feet. Crappie are good on bridge columns and shallow brush on jigs and minnows. Largemouth bass are good at daylight on frogs in the pads and mid morning and evening on shallow cranks, flukes and smaller rattle traps on shallow points.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good near docks and rocks on crankbaits and quick moving baits.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass are down, but the grass and ledges are still producing the most. Small swimbaits on underspins are catching schooling bass. Bass are schooling in the marinas chasing �¾ inch bait fish.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles with minnows and jigs in 12-16 feet of water. Bass are good in 6-7 feet of water on grass and shaded structure with soft plastics. Crappie have been in two main patterns with most fish 20 feet deep, but there is a good number of fish in 8-12 feet of water on brush piles. Bass are great at dawn and dusk on topwater, but this bite shuts off very quickly.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 17 feet of water on brush piles or standing timber with live bait. Black bass are slow. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on soft plastics or crankbaits in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 8-10 feet of water on brush.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-30 feet on minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on main lake rocky points with deep water access are holding fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Many anglers are catching crappie at the oil derricks.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been slow and scattered. Some bass are schooling. Crappie are slow as well.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, some areas of the lake with creek inflows are showing heavy signs of stain.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Mayflies are hatching, so expect some topwater bass action. Bass are fair on soft plastics in the cuts, or with frogs over grass. Crappie are fair with jigs in flooded timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Lake Bastrop is going strong for schooling bass. Later move off the north end of the dam and throw at the schooling bass blowing up the water. You can also throw a small ball head, new jig head with a natural shad colored tiny swimbait, a fluke, and Texas or Carolina-rigged for deeper bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water, or suspended in 15 feet of water with minnows. Black bass are feeding early on shad patterns around grass and retaining walls. Main lake points are good for bass using clouser type patterns. Bass are good on points in 18-22 feet of water using deep water baits like deep diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs. Sand bass and black bass schooling together near the dam, and bridges.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing seems to be slower than normal, but picking up by mid morning. When the sun rises, target offshore bass in 12-20 feet of water on humps, brush piles and pond dams with Carolina rigs and Texas rigs with creature baits and yum dingers.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good around weed lines using plastics worms and jigs.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass catches up to 6.77 pounds are Fair on Hag’s cyclone craw in Juice Box on the ledges, or with shaky heads in 6-20 feet in the habitats around the main lake and points. Crappie are fair around docks with brush on minnows in 12-18 feet. White bass to 12 inches are fair on crappie jigs, trolling crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass catches can be had early in the morning.
reports.by: The Bait Barn

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair, but can be caught off main lake points or ledges, and shallow rock piles in 8-12 feet of water. Crappie are good in 25 feet of water on timber and brush with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Lake Buchanan is still fishing good for bass.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling throughout the lake and can be caught with a fluke, or small topwater bait.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good early in the morning or late in the afternoon on long extended points with watermelon colored soft plastic worms and flukes. Crappie are biting in brush piles in 20-30 feet of water on minnows.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on big worms and creature baits around structure and under docks when the sun is out. Some anglers are jigging spoons too aggressively, get more hits with a calmer jigging motion, white or chartreuse slabs from MT Pockets have been working well. Crappie are in or around structure and timber in 12-21 feet using minnows, jigs, and or hair jigs, the bite has been very light, and have shut off as quickly as you get one in the boat, but some are getting a great catch.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
