reports.text: Bass are excellent early until about 8 a.m. on shallow points with square bill crankbaits and underspins. Then target bass in 15-25 feet of water with deep diving crankbaits.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the mornings in 1-3 feet of water in the shallow grass with frogs and swimbaits, and Viper XP swim jigs. Bass are feeding in 10-12 feet where the thermocline is not present. Look for schooling bass in the open water and creeks as shad hatch is in full swing. Also, check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork continues to be excellent as we get deeper into the summer pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow to fair on crankbaits and soft plastics near main lake points and near deeper docks. Crappie are fair to good on small minnows and jigs fished midlake near submerged timber in about 15-20 feet down.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on plastic worms fished around cover up river near the island. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished in 6-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good Try closures around edges of grass during the day. Bead heads will tempt bream and bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass as with other species have spread out, but can be caught on structure with worms and grubs. Crappie are plentiful if you can find them in the eddy and areas protected by current holding tight to structure being caught in 10-14 feet of water on small hand tied jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with the best bite around the north end of the dam on rocks of the overflow, and in Game Warden Cove in 4-11 feet of water on trees near the rocky shoreline. Smaller fish are biting topwaters, and bigger fish were caught on square bill crankbaits for jerkbaits for schooling bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water on crankbaits and soft plastics, and in 8-14 feet of water on brush with soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie on deep submerged brush and or trees. Bass bite is fair with small fish shallow, and the occasional big fish on deeper points or channel edges.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-24 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass and keeper hybrids are fair on humps and points in 10-25 feet of water with slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 6-26 feet of water. Bass fishing is slow while the water level continues to be high.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and largemouth bass are holding to the same patterns. Largemouth bass Crappie are good on offshore brush in 11-14 feet.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on lipless crankbaits, swimbaits with underspin and senko weightless worm. Crappie remains good in 20-25 feet of water with fish suspended in brush piles with minnows as the best bait. Catfish are in the deeper waters along with the crappie using live bait on rod and reel.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on heavy weighted Carolina rigs, deep crankbaits, medium to deep diving crankbaits. Bass are set up in large groups on hard spots like shell bottom. Crappie are good with swarms of fish on brush piles with any colored crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on big swimbaits and Carolina rigs on timber lines and the bottom of shallow points on clumps of grass. Crappie are good cruising around the timber lines with some brush piles with live minnows or chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 7 pounds, a couple of fish a little over 10 pounds and one over 13 pounds. Crappie very good suspended and deeper trees 6-18 feet best on minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports of quality bass 5 pounds and more being caught using deep crankbaits and soft plastics, and Untamed Sportsman worms on a �¾ ounce heads.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Boathouse patterns should be best for bass.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still biting great on live bait 8-10 feet of water and brush piles and dead trees.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on timber lines with big swimbaits, and small paddle tail swimbaits. Crappie are slow live minnows or natural colored crappie jigs on standing timber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are still slow in 20-30 feet of water using live shad or small slabs and jigs white, and silver are good colors. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: To catch fish in deep schools throw your slab out, let it sink then reel 10 turns and let it drop back to the bottom. Crappie are fair in 24-35 feet deep on brush, or suspended on bridge piles with the best bite on minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass can be found up the Creek Arms on Points in 10-15 feet of water with slabs.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville Marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnow, over brush, 8-16 feet of water on the main lake.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow, but anglers have reported some success for bass with soft plastics such as the Hags Cheat code and craws. Slabs and Bomber Slab spoons.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair frequently changing locations, so keep that perseverance and soft plastics in the tackle box. Crappie, catfish and white bass are fair.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has been spotty as fish continue to adjust after a total loss of the hydrilla crop due to flooding in May.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Live bait, slabs or topwaters along river channels and flats in 30-50 feet of water. Crappie fishing is slow using jigs on brush piles and in docks. Look in 15-20 feet of water with minnows and crappie nibbles. Bass fishing is slow with topwaters early and slow soft plastics throughout the day on structure and near docks. Stripers are good with slabs fishing under the smaller topwater fish in 30-60 feet of water in the middle of the lake.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is just slow. Bass fishing is still fair. There are few small fish being caught out deeper in 18-25 feet on drop shot and spoons, these fish are small and most are Kentucky bass.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: A pattern should emerge for bass. Check newly submerged shorelines casting a topwater or moving bait, if bait has pushed shallow bass will follow.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Night fishing is good for catfish and crappie in the lights. Crappie are good using minnows and jigs on brush in 16 feet of water. Bass are fair biting off the barge with a variety of baits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: For the first couple hours try for bigger fish around the shores, then target schooling bass. Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water on chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-20 feet on the north end of the lake. Largemouth bass fishing is slow.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass fishing is fair on main lake points and secondary points 15-25 feet with deep water access are holding fish.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on points, or off docks where bass are seeking out that secondary cover. Crappie are biting on brush piles with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been biting well this week with the cloud cover.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Bass are more active Bass are fair on soft plastics in the cuts, or with frogs over grass. Crappie are fair with jigs in flooded timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with black and green jigs or minnows. Crappie are good at night under the bridges with minnows. Black bass are feeding early on shad patterns around grass and retaining walls. Main lake points are good for bass using clouser type patterns. Bass are good on points in 18-22 feet of water using deep water baits like deep diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs. Sand bass and black bass schooling together near the dam, and bridges.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been steady with the best bite on offshore points and brush piles or man made structures.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with the best action early morning and late afternoon along deeper rocky shores and salt cedars in 5-8 feet of water with slow moving baits and soft plastics. Crappie and white bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good around weed lines on plastic worms and jigs.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing continues to be good! On main lake humps, ledges, ridges have been good with live bait and slabs catching fish. Largemouth bass have been good on topwaters early in the morning, and with flat billed crankbaits of finesse baits near lake points later in the day.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.15 pounds are slow on Hag’s cyclone craws in Juice Box, shaky heads in 6-20 feet in the habitats around the main lake and top waters early in 2-8 feet on the flats. Crappie are slow around docks with brush on minnows in 10-14 feet. White bass to 12 inches are slow on crankbaits and crappie jigs under the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass can be caught off main lake points or ledges, and shallow rock piles in 8-12 feet of water. Crappie are good in 25 feet of water on timber and brush with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Captain Aaron Dick, One Up Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Normally bass move into the river to deep cuts following bait, if this happens a shaky head, dropshot, or a light Texas rig.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: There is a good bass topwater bite in the morning around isolated grass and rock.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and white bass are good early in the morning at daylight on midlake points and drop offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 13-22 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Hit up seawalls close to points in depths of 5-18 feet and cast rattle traps, spoons, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Cast topwater baits into bass surfacing, jumping out of the water. Largemouth bass are good on topwater lures.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is good fishing offshore structure with brush on it using Texas rigs, Carolina rigs, and crankbaits. Some anglers are jigging spoons too aggressively, get more hits with a calmer jigging motion, white or chartreuse slabs from MT Pockets has been working well.
reports.by: Roy Crush Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 25-30 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Bass are good on deep water points and boat docks with deep jigs, diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early until about 8 a.m. on shallow points with square bill crankbaits and underspins. Then target bass in 15-25 feet of water with deep diving crankbaits.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow while the moon is fuller, and fish are more active at night. Bass are hitting topwaters and shallow streamers fished over flooded milfoil and hydrilla. Look for schooling bass in the open water and creeks as shad hatch is in full swing. Also, check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork continues to be excellent as we get deeper into the summer pattern.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie and good on deep brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow to fair on slabs and spinners from Decordova to Indian Harbor. Largemouth bass are slow to fair on crankbaits and soft plastics worked near main lake points and near shaded docks later in the day. Crappie continue to be good on small minnows and jigs fished near suspended timber mid-lake and near bridge pilings.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits and crankbaits fished around shallow cover. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished over brush in 8-12 feet of water. White bass are good on slab spoons fished over main lake humps and points.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are chasing poppers and shallow streamers on the main lake points. Bead heads will tempt bream and bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are hanging tight to structure, mainly in cypress stumps, and drop-offs in the morning biting grubs and worms. Crappie are scattered in 6-10 feet of water in the rivers and creeks being caught in small artificial jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Solid summer pattern is holding steady for the bass. Bass are good with schooling activity starting to pick up. Follow the shad to find the bass. There is still some bass in the bushes along the banks pitching Texas rigged worms and jigs, or wacky rigs. Bass are good on brush piles on points on the south end of the lake in 15-25 feet of water with deep running crankbaits, jigs, wacky worms and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Mike Stroman, R & R Marine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-24 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good skipping docks with wacky rigged and Texas-rigged worms, or throwing swimbaits and crankbaits around any grass you find will catch some also.

reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report

reports.by: Hambone Guide service

reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good for catches 2-5 pounds on deep diving crankbaits, Carolina rigs and dropshots. Crappie are good on brush piles with live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on big swimbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are good on brush piles with live minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report

reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report

reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and artificial grubs. Bass are fair on soft plastic artificials. Bluegill are excellent at the boathouse dock on crappie bites and worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report

reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair, but some decent fish can be caught with perseverance early in the morning with soft plastics. Very little activity for crappie, catfish and white bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been very hit or miss for both white bass and for largemouth bass thanks to the atypical (cool, damp) weather we have and will continue to experience since Thursday, 18 July through to at least Tuesday, 30 July. With a near 100% loss of hydrilla due to May's flooding, largemouth bass are consolidating on the few remaining rock and wood structures, as well as on topographic features.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: A lot of fish are being caught on the surface early in the morning as they feed on schools of threadfin shad, so slabs and swimbaits are working best in these situations. Crappie have been decent on brush piles and bridge pylons in 12-18 feet. The largemouth bass bite has been decent on rooster frogs early in the morning in the pads.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Swimbaits and slabs are working along the banks early in the morning as well. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows fishing brush piles in 15-25 feet of water. Bass are slow on topwaters early along the bluffs and soft plastics in the backs of the coves midday. Stripers are good with slabs fishing under the smaller topwater fish in 30-60 feet of water in the middle of the lake.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures are back down in the high 80s, so when the weather finally settles the bass fishing should improve during the day with all the freshwater. The crappie fishing has been slow but should improve.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in a consistent summer pattern. Continue to downsize baits to match the small 1 inch baitfish the bass are feeding on. There is decent bass bite with early morning schooling around deep marinas and coves.

Bass are good on points in 18-22 feet of water using deep water baits like deep diving crankbaits, dropshots and Texas rigs. Sand bass and black bass schooling together near the dam, and bridges.

reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on topwater lures.

reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Fish can be caught on spoons or slabs. Crappie are good on main lake brush piles, or in 4-18 feet of water on timber. Fish are not schooled up, so hit several trees for a mess of crappie.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fairly slow in the mornings, but there is a shaky head bite with yum dingers in both sizes on timber in 5-7 feet on breaklines. Black bass are chasing topwater patterns early in the day and later in the day when it is dark. Check out the brush piles as big bass are using them to feed on crappie. Lake Fork crappie fishing is in full time summer pattern. Huge numbers of black crappie are loading up at the base of trees, on main lake points and lay downs. There are still good numbers of white crappie on brush piles and in trees. Larger soft plastics should still work on bigger white crappies that are solo on timber.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in deep brush piles on minnows and jigs. Bass are biting early and late.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in numbers with an occasional bigger fish to 7 pounds. Largemouth bass are best on crankbaits and soft plastics worked near docks and main lake points. Crappie are fair to good on jigs and minnows on submerged timber midlake.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have really bounced back on stumps and riprap early and later in the day. Crappie are slowly getting hungry on structure in the main channels eating small jigs in 8–14 feet of water. White bass are good during the day on humps on the south end either vertical jigging Duck tracker slabs with Texan teasers, or trolling in 12-16 feet of water with small spoons.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report

reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great on brush piles in 15 feet of water and submerged timber or hard structure in 9-22 feet of water. Crappie are biting 1/32-1/8 ounce jigs or minnows. Black bass are in 3-20 feet of water with white and chartreuse spinnerbaits early in the morning. Any standing timber 10 feet off the bank might hold bass as well as an ambush point. If you get lucky, they will stay under the boat and you can finish your limit with 1 ounce slabs in chartreuse or white or silver. Do not be surprised if you catch crappies while targeting the gills.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on humps and points in 15-25 feet of water with slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 10-34 feet of water. Bass fishing is slow while the water level continues to be high.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass bite is excellent in 10-20 feet of water with white and chartreuse Ducktracker slabs.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Found quality bass holding tight to submerged timber with a Texas rigged Mag-worm. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on large glide baits and swimbaits. Crappie are good for size but quantity is low, on brush piles with chartreuse crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been good on white chatterbaits and spinnerbaits early morning and evening. Midday flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water is the ticket to catch shaded up largemouth bass. Crappie were good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on chartreuse slabs. Crappie are fair on minnows in the flooded timber around the edge of the lake and on brush piles. Largemouth bass are fair on crawfish jigs near the dam.
reports.by: Clay Major, Major Guide Service

reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with three fish stringers weighing in at 15 pounds. Crappie and catfish are fair.

reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: We are catching them on slabs and swim baits when this happens. The crappie bite has been slow. The largemouth bite has been good with white frogs early in the pads then switching over to crankbaits and brush houses the sun comes up and super shallow on dock legs and riprap.

reports.text: Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows using electronics to locate active fish on brush in 20 feet of water near points and drop offs. Bass fishing is slow along the bluffs on live shad as the fry are abundant and fish are feeding hard early. reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.text: Hot weather has slowed the bass bite during the day. Target bass slowly working a Texas or Carolina rig. Crappie are still hit-or-miss over the lake, but it seems like the mid lake area from around the bridge north a few miles has been the best.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slow using jigs on structure and brush piles in 15-20 feet of water. Bass fishing is slow using topwaters early on main lake points and the mouths of coves. When this bite ends live bait and slabs are producing catches.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Guadaliupe bass can be caught on bluff walls between marinas. Bass are very active chasing shad in the marinas. Bass are good in the shaded areas of the marinas biting small swimbaits, and slowly working small topwaters. Continue to downsize baits to match the small 1 inch baitfish the bass are feeding on. Lake Travis bass fishing is good early in the mornings and late in the evenings and dark.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good using minnows and jigs on brush in 16 feet of water. Bass are good on crankbaits, plastic worms and topwater frogs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwater frogs and worms early in the day. Most bass are in 10-25 feet of water with some schooling almost every trip. Lake Decker is fishing well for bass. Big largemouth bass can be mixed in, so be ready.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide
